scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r12 dummy interfaces lo1, lo2, lo3
Mechanism: r12's four /24 loopbacks live on separate Linux
  interfaces (lo, lo1, lo2, lo3) — that's the workaround for
  FRR eigrpd only advertising one prefix per interface. When
  lo1/lo2/lo3 go down, EIGRP withdraws those three prefixes;
  102.1.1.0/24 (on the real `lo`) stays advertised. R11
  withdraws them upstream into OSPF.
Localization: r12
Root cause: dummy interfaces lo1/lo2/lo3 are down on r12
Fix: `ip link set lo1 up; ip link set lo2 up; ip link set lo3 up`
  on r12
scenario.fix_spec:
`ip link set lo1 up; ip link set lo2 up; ip link set lo3 up`
  on r12

agent.diagnosis_text:
The affected subsystem is the EIGRP source on r12: three dummy loopback
interfaces (lo1, lo2, lo3) that host the 102.1.2.1/24, 102.1.3.1/24, and
102.1.4.1/24 connected prefixes are currently in Linux link-DOWN state.
Only the main loopback lo (102.1.1.1/24) is UP, which is why 102.1.1.0/24
remains visible while the other three vanish.

The mechanism is straightforward: FRR's eigrpd on r12 only places a
connected network into its EIGRP topology table when the underlying
interface is UP and the address is reachable as a connected route. With
lo1/lo2/lo3 DOWN, r12's routing table carries no entry for those three
/24s, and r12's EIGRP topology confirms they are entirely absent from its
own table. R11 therefore never receives (or eventually withdraws) those
three prefixes, does not redistribute them into OSPF area 3, and r1 loses
them from its RIB. The EIGRP adjacency between r11 and r12 is still up
because it is maintained over the eth0/EE segment (112.0.0.0/8), which is
completely unaffected.

The root cause is that r12's startup script (r12.startup) successfully
created lo1, lo2, lo3 as dummy interfaces, brought them UP, and assigned
the /24 addresses — but a subsequent fault injection issued
`ip link set lo1/lo2/lo3 down`, silently removing those connected routes
from r12's RIB and EIGRP without tearing the EIGRP neighbor session.

Corrective fix: on r12, run `ip link set lo1 up; ip link set lo2 up;
ip link set lo3 up`. The three connected routes will re-enter r12's routing
table, r12's eigrpd will re-advertise them to r11, r11 will redistribute
them into OSPF, and r1 will reinstall 102.1.2.0/24, 102.1.3.0/24, and
102.1.4.0/24 within seconds.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies r12 as the affected device multiple times.
Agent explicitly identifies the loopback dummy interfaces lo1/lo2/lo3 on r12 as being down.
The report explicitly notes a partial withdrawal: lo1/lo2/lo3 (three /24s) are link-DOWN and withdrawn while the main lo (102.1.1.0/24) remains advertised.
The agent instructs to bring lo1, lo2, and lo3 up on r12 (ip link set ... up), which exactly matches the expected remediation.

The agent's log contains commands and outputs (r12's ip/route/eigrp topology, r12 startup, r11 neighbor, r1 OSPF/RIB notes) that support the claim that lo1/lo2/lo3 are down and their prefixes absent; the inferences about connected routes being withdrawn from EIGRP and upstream OSPF redistribution follow logically and essential checks were performed.
